set.prevailing_wage_basis: 24 CFR 983.153(c)(1)-(2) (PBV program, development requirements): for development involving nine or more PBV contract units, the owner and its contractors must pay Davis-Bacon wages to laborers and mechanics and comply with CWHSSA and 29 CFR part 5; the PHA monitors compliance. Applies from proposal submission or PHA board resolution if work starts before the Agreement. Existing-housing PBV and projects under 9 contract units are not covered by this rule; RAD conversions follow the RAD Notice labor standards, not checked in this pass. https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/983.153
set.layering_notes: Fresno County splits housing work three ways: the Department of Public Works and Planning, Community Development Division (ComDev) runs the Urban County HUD programs, PLHA and the annual Affordable Housing Development NOFO; the County Administrative Office's new Office of Housing and Homelessness (OHH, created November 18, 2025) administers HHAP, the Continuum of Care and Transitional Rent and is absorbing housing programs from Behavioral Health and ComDev (Phase 2 approved November 3, 2026); and the Department of Behavioral Health co-applies for Homekey+ and NPLH and funds BHSA housing. Fresno Housing (the joint City and County Housing Authorities) is the dominant developer and voucher source. The City of Fresno and Clovis are separate entitlements with their own programs (Pass 3). fresnocountyca.gov and fresnohousing.org open normally; Board records are on fresnocounty.legistar.com and the Legistar web API client 'fresnocounty'. Fresno Housing is both the PHA and the county's most prolific developer (over 2,100 units since 2010, $600 million of development), so most County PBVs flow to its own tax credit and RAD deals; a third-party developer's realistic path is a joint venture with Fresno Housing as co-general partner, as at Sendero Commons' sister project Davu Village, or a competitive RFP when one is published. Davis-Bacon applies to PBV development activity involving nine or more contract units (24 CFR 983.153(c)(2)). Source is the 2027 Annual Plan for the Housing Authority of the County of Fresno (draft) on fresnohousing.org; selection rules from the 2027 County Administrative Plan chapter 17.
set.audit_note: Tier 3: prevailing wage set true from 24 CFR 983.153(c) for PBV development of 9+ contract units. RAD conversion labor standards not separately verified; check the current RAD Notice for RAD-only rehab.

reason: 24 CFR 983.153(c)(2) requires Davis-Bacon wages for PBV development involving nine or more contract units.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: No program rule found. The City RLF Agreement form (Council item 26-440, Park at South Stadium) requires compliance with prevailing wage laws only 'as may be applicable' (sections 5.4 and 7.14) and the staff reports and resolutions for Helm Lofts, Uptown and South Stadium are silent. Coverage then rests on Labor Code 1720(b) (public funds, including below-market loans) and depends on 1720(c) facts, such as (c)(5)(E) for below-market loans with 40% of units at 80% AMI or less for 20+ years and (c)(3) de minimis, so it is project-specific. https://agendas.fresno.gov/en/legislation/id-26-440-21137 ; https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720
set.layering_notes: Short-term construction money, not permanent soft debt: it must be taken out at conversion, so it suits 4% LIHTC or mixed-income deals with a permanent loan sized to repay. Pairs with City PLHA, LHTF and FHS land in the Downtown/Chinatown area, and with the TOD height and density bonus. RLF capital is State money: $20 million of the State's $250 million Downtown Fresno appropriation (FY 2025-26 installment, Resolution 2025-256) plus a further $5 million appropriated in 2026 for a $25 million fund (Council item 25-1713). The executed RLF Agreement form (item 26-440) nonetheless contains boilerplate federal compliance language; confirm with the City whether any federal cross-cutters attach.
set.audit_note: Tier 3: prevailing wage left unclear. RLF Agreement says prevailing wage applies 'as may be applicable'; outcome depends on Labor Code 1720(b) and 1720(c) project facts. The Round 2 NOFA document itself (PlanetBids 12601560) was not readable.

reason: The RLF Agreement and staff reports defer to prevailing wage law 'as may be applicable' with no stated program rule, so coverage depends on Labor Code 1720(c) project facts.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: No program rule found; Ordinance 2008-51 (fee deferral to certificate of occupancy) says nothing on prevailing wage. Coverage would rest only on Labor Code 1720(b)(4) (fees or obligations paid, reduced, waived or forgiven), and whether a deferral with no reduction counts, plus the 1720(c)(3) de minimis test ($600,000 and 2% of project cost), depends on project facts. No DIR determination on point was located. https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720
set.audit_note: Tier 3: prevailing wage left unclear. The only basis is Labor Code 1720(b)(4); a pure deferral may not be a reduction or waiver, and the de minimis exemption in 1720(c)(3) may apply. Project-specific.

reason: The ordinance has no prevailing wage term and the only basis is Labor Code 1720(b)(4), whose application to a pure deferral depends on 1720(c) facts.
